build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: Platform movement is tight and expressive: the knight moves left/right with controlled acceleration, jumps with a smooth gravity arc supporting variable height or early-release control, flips to face movement direction, and lands reliably on platforms without jittering through walls or floors. Score 0 if movement is grid-snapped, floaty, lacks gravity, or uses pass-through placeholder collision.

Advanced traversal mechanics gate progression: wall-cling, wall-jump, and dash each have distinct input, timing, cooldown or limits, and level geometry that requires them to advance. Score 0 if abilities are absent or purely cosmetic.

Melee combat is a stateful system: nail slash has a frontal hitbox and recovery, enemies take visible damage and can damage the player, invincibility frames prevent repeated hits, kills award geo and soul, and dead enemies are removed from collision. Score 0 if combat is only an animation or enemies are inert.

Soul, healing, health, and death form a survival loop: mask health decreases on damage, soul meter fills from combat, holding focus consumes soul to heal one mask during a vulnerable window, zero health triggers defeat with geo penalty. Score 0 if health or soul are missing or healing is free/instant.

Stage resolution and persistence are connected: the player starts from a checkpoint, reaches an endpoint to clear a stage, unlocks the next stage in save data, returns to the kingdom map, and load/continue restores progress. Score 0 if stages are disconnected scenes or progress never saves.

A kingdom map presents at least three named stages in a linear progression with locked/unlocked states enforced — later stages require earlier completion. Score 0 if there is one level or locked stages can be entered freely.

Non-boss stages contain multiple connected rooms with varied platform layouts, verticality, hazards, enemy locks or barriers, and wall-cling sections that differ across rooms. Score 0 if the level is one flat screen or all rooms are cosmetic duplicates.

At least three enemy types exist that are visually distinct and functionally different — varying in movement, attack style, HP, speed, range, or room-lock role. Score 0 if enemies are clones or all share identical stats and behavior.

A boss encounter occupies its own room with a large health indicator, at least three attack patterns with readable telegraphs, a defeat condition, and a victory reward. Score 0 if there is no boss or the boss repeats one simple attack.

Metroidvania systems beyond combat are present: geo economy, checkpoints, ability-gated routes, stage preview information, collectibles, or environmental storytelling — at least three such systems are implemented and visible. Score 0 if the game is only a linear fight corridor with no progression context.

Platforming readability is strong: safe ground, walls, thorn hazards, pits, wall-cling surfaces, dash gaps, checkpoints, and endpoints are distinguishable at 1280x720. The player can plan jumps without guessing collision boundaries. Score 0 if terrain and hazards blend together or important surfaces are only labeled with text.

Combat and survival information is always readable: mask health, soul meter, geo count, enemy damage state, boss HP, and healing state are visible without opening hidden panels. Score 0 if health, soul, or boss HP are missing or ambiguous.

Action feedback is visible: slash, enemy hit, player hit, i-frame flash, geo pickup, soul gain, focus heal, death, checkpoint save, and boss telegraph each produce observable feedback. Score 0 if actions happen silently or are communicated only by debug text.

Menus and navigation are usable: title start/load, kingdom map, locked-stage indicators, pause/retry, and stage-clear/defeat flows have readable hierarchy, spacing, and contrast. Score 0 if UI clips, overlaps, or looks like raw development labels.

The game has a coherent melancholic underground art direction: title, map, rooms, knight, enemies, boss, HUD, and effects share cold blue or deep purple tones, high-contrast silhouettes, and a ruined-kingdom mood. Score 0 if visible gameplay relies on ColorRect primitives, default HTML 引擎 UI, or bright off-brief placeholder colors. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Environment art uses textured or illustrated cavern/ruin tiles, layered background depth, and readable platform edges. Each stage has a distinct visual identity while staying in the same world. Score 0 if rooms are flat fills or untextured rectangles.

Character, enemy, and boss art are finished sprites with recognizable silhouettes: the knight, regular enemies, and boss each have distinct designs, scale, palette, and animation poses. Score 0 if the player or enemies are boxes, circles, or generic icons.

Animation supports the action-platformer feel: idle, run, jump, fall, wall-cling, slash, enemy patrol/attack, hit reaction, death, and boss attacks use multi-frame animation, tweening, or particles. Score 0 if major interactions are single-frame snaps or static sprites sliding around.

UI chrome and atmospheric polish: title logo, map nodes, mask icons, soul meter, geo counter, boss HP, result panels, room transitions, particles, glow, and fog use themed frames, icons, or illustrated elements rather than naked default widgets. Score 0 if UI is mostly unstyled default labels and the game lacks atmospheric effects.
